name: Six Senses AMAALA
positioning: Village-inspired wellness resort on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, within the AMAALA destination
best_for: Wellness travelers wanting a spa with a Longevity Center, thermal areas and multi-day programs
Couples and families wanting a pool suite or a villa with up to four bedrooms
Travelers drawn to beaches, coral reefs and sailing

facts.text: Six Senses AMAALA is a village-inspired resort that blends its suites, villas and branded residences into the natural terrain.
AMAALA spans over 1,600 square miles (4,144 square kilometers) of protected coastline on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea.
Guests choose from pool suites, villas with one to four bedrooms, and branded residences.
Interiors feature calming tones, natural wood and layered textiles.
Spa treatment rooms open onto private terraces, and the spa has a Watsu pool and a sound dome.
Wellness includes signature massages, hammam rituals, family treatments, daily yoga and fitness classes, and multi-day programs.
Soraya, the signature dinner restaurant atop the Mesa, has panoramic bay views and blends Japanese and Latin American cooking with Red Sea produce.
The non-alcoholic beverage program features fermented drinks, botanical infusions and probiotic tonics.
The Corallium Marine Life Institute offers marine exhibits, and the AMAALA Yacht Club hosts a sailing community.
Experiences range from desert adventures to reefs.

highlights.text: The clifftop Mesa crowns the resort, framed by beaches, a mangrove-fringed lagoon and coral reefs.
The spa is a desert oasis sheltered between sloping walls, with lush vegetation, pools and waterfalls.
The Longevity Center features recovery treatments, and separate male and female thermal areas include saunas, a salt room and vitality pools.
Accommodation is inspired by traditional Saudi coastal villages and built with locally sourced materials.

considerations.text: The beverage program is non-alcoholic, built on fermented drinks, botanical infusions and probiotic tonics.
WhataHotel notes the remote destination requires long-haul travel for most international guests.
WhataHotel notes limited off-resort attractions given the secluded coastal location.
